findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height version
findings.body:
Ruby has no method overloading. The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it at line 145.

Existing callers that pass width and height separately now break:
- A call like `downsize(path, path, w, h, opts)` raises ArgumentError because it passes 5 arguments to a method that accepts 3–4.
- A call like `downsize(path, path, w, h)` binds `h` (an Integer) to `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` then raises a TypeError.

This breaks avatar and emoji downsizing done in `Upload.create_for`. The two variants need distinct names, or one method that accepts either form.

findings.title: Downsize result ignored; animated GIFs get an invalid gifsicle argument
findings.body:
The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If ImageMagick or gifsicle fails, the loop keeps retrying a no-op up to 5 times and then uploads the oversized file anyway.

With `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a .gif file, `optimize` routes to `resize_instructions_animated`. That produces `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid gifsicle geometry. Every attempt therefore fails, and large animated GIFs are never reduced.

The loop should stop on failure, and it should pass a geometry gifsicle understands, such as concrete pixel dimensions.

findings.title: In-place conversion may leave `tempfile.size` and the open handle stale
findings.body:
The image is rewritten in place at `tempfile.path` by `convert` and then by ImageOptim. ImageOptim, and possibly convert, write a new file and rename it over the path, which gives the path a new inode.

`Tempfile#size` stats the already-open file descriptor, which still points at the old, now-unlinked inode. In that case:
- the `while` condition never sees the reduced size, so all 5 iterations run, each shrinking the image by another 80%;
- `tempfile.size` passed to `Upload.create_for` reports the original size rather than the stored file's size.

Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` for the size checks and the size argument.

findings.title: SVG uploads are run through ImageMagick raster resize
findings.body:
`FileHelper.is_image?` matches .svg files. An SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` will be passed to `convert ... -resize 80%` with an .svg output path. That rasterizes or mangles the vector file, or fails, instead of leaving it alone.

Elsewhere SVGs are explicitly copied rather than resized (see `OptimizedImage.create_for`). SVGs should be excluded here too.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores the attachment size setting
findings.body:
The client check previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for both images and attachments.

This has two effects:
- Sites that set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload larger attachments, because the client rejects them.
- Attachments between the site limit and 10MB are no longer rejected client-side, so users wait for the upload and then get a server error.

Only the image limit should be relaxed, since only images are auto-downsized. The 413 message at line 246 likewise reports 10MB regardless of the actual server limit.

findings.title: API URL downloads now capped at 10MB regardless of type
findings.body:
The download limit for API-provided URLs is now hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type.

Attachments allowed by `max_attachment_size_kb` beyond 10MB can no longer be fetched. When a download exceeds the cap, the `rescue nil` swallows the error and leaves `tempfile` nil. `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` at line 72 then raises NoMethodError instead of returning a proper size error.

findings.title: No tests for automatic downsizing or the changed downsize API
findings.body:
The PR adds a downsizing loop and changes the `OptimizedImage.resize`/`downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but includes no specs.

A spec exercising `downsize` with width/height arguments, or the upload controller with an oversized image, would have caught the method redefinition that breaks existing callers.
